note: The seam catalogue (fe-country-split-plan §4.3, §4.9), the base product's extension points and the protected list (§4.11 rule 3). A seam is a base product file with a neutral default that a country may replace by a file at the seam's conventional path: `country` is relative to the country's fe/, `base` (the default) and `replaces` (the file a build compiles in its place) to the base product's fe/. Set-up adds a fileReplacements entry, or for `option` that angular.json option, for every seam whose country file exists, in the configurations named (`every` for all of the application's). `generated` are seams the kit fills itself, with no country file. `hooks` are injection tokens a country provides its own implementations of in country.providers.ts, beside the base product's defaults. `slots` are named places in base product templates (`<app-slot name="…" />`) where a country registers a component with provideSlot and a lazy loader; a slot's default renders nothing. Every hook and slot is a promise the base product keeps across versions, added only where a country needs one. `protected` are globs, relative to the base product's fe/, of files no country override may replace; an override (niord-country.json `overrides`) may replace any other TypeScript, JavaScript or JSON file of an application's src/app/ but a spec or a seam's file.

seams.description: The development build's backends: the local stack, /rest through the dev proxy, Keycloak at http://localhost:8080/auth.
The local build's backends, as the development build's.

The test deployment's: /rest and /auth on its own origin, mode test and production true, so a test build neither registers the dev routes nor lets the e2e test's Keycloak token stub take Keycloak's place. Set-up does not check it.

Production: production true, without which a production bundle lets the e2e test's Keycloak token stub take Keycloak's place and compiles in the dev routes; apiBaseUrl /rest, keycloak.url /auth and map.wmsUrl, if set, /wms/ — origin-relative. Set-up checks both.
The public site's country configuration and the footer component it names.
The public site's index.html: its title and the branding icons it links.

The administration app's behaviour hooks and component slots: provideCountry(), returning the providers of the hooks below and the country's provideSlot registrations, added at the root injector beside the base product's own. The default adds nothing.

The administration app's own pages: the default export, Routes, loaded lazily after every base route. Each top-level entry has canMatch: [roleGuard] with a non-empty data.rolesRequired, data: { public: true }, or is a redirect; any other is left out and logged. The default has none.

The administration app's own menu entries: COUNTRY_MENU_ENTRIES, each { after (the base item it follows: messages, editor, schedule, admin or sysadmin), labelKey (a country.* key), icon (a registered ng-icons name), routerLink, roles (any one of them; [] for everyone) }. The default has none.
The public site's own pages: the default export, Routes, loaded lazily as the layout's last child, after every base route; every one public, as the site is. The default has none.
The public site's component slots and hooks: provideCountry(), returning the country's provideSlot registrations. The default adds nothing.

generated.description: The language configuration, made from the manifest and each pack's pack.json.
The language configuration, made from the manifest and each pack's pack.json.
The brand tokens: the styles array names styles/tokens.<country>.css, and styles/fonts.<country>.css when the country has one, where the base product's names tokens.active.css.
The brand tokens, as the administration app's.

hooks.description: How a message's promulgation of one service is shown: { serviceId, component }, multi. The base product registers navtex, twitter, safetynet and audio; a country adds one per service of its own with { provide: PROMULGATION_RENDERERS, useValue, multi: true }.

How the editor edits a promulgation of one service: { serviceId, component }, multi, as the renderers. The base product registers navtex, twitter, safetynet and audio; a country adds the editor of each service of its own.

slots.description: The end of the front page's welcome panel, below the sign-in prompt.
Every page of the public site, between the main content and the footer.
